label: rem:hyperbolic-volume-degeneracy-prior-art
title: Prior art: hyperbolic volume does not determine the manifold
html:
By Jørgensen and Thurston, only finitely many orientable hyperbolic 3-manifolds have a given volume v; write N(v) for that number. Hodgson and Masai record that it is often larger than one [hodgson2012, \S 1, pp. 1--2]. At the lowest cusped volume v_\omega = 2.029883\ldots there are exactly two cusped manifolds, the figure-eight knot complement and its sister m003 (Cao–Meyerhoff). For link complements in S^3 the count grows at least exponentially: for each n \ge 3 there are at least 2^n/(2n) hyperbolic link complements of volume 4nV_8, where V_8 is the volume of the regular ideal octahedron [hodgson2012, Thm 8.5, p. 22].

For the volume of the Reeb-bundle complement this sets a scope: \mathrm{Vol}(K) is a well-defined invariant of each knot or link, but it is not an identifying label. Two different link complements can have the same volume, so a quantity that depends on K only through \mathrm{Vol}(K) cannot tell them apart. In particular \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) is also the volume of the sister manifold m003. The paper says nothing about the other factors of the mass law, so it neither supports nor rules out any QOU mass assignment.
